from rich.ansi import re_ansi

test_cases = [
    "\x1b7",
    "\x1b8",
    "\x1b0",
    "\x1b?",
    "\x1b@",
    "\x1b[m",
    "\x1b]test\x1b\\",
]

for tc in test_cases:
    match = re_ansi.search(tc)
    print(f"Text: {repr(tc)}, Match: {repr(match.group(0)) if match else 'None'}, Groups: {match.groups() if match else 'None'}")

from rich.ansi import _ansi_tokenize, _AnsiToken

def test_ansi_tokenize():
    test_cases = [
        ("Hello\x1b7World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b8World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b0World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b?World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b@World", "HelloWorld"),
        ("Hello\x1b[mWorld", "HelloWorld"), # This is an SGR, but it is handled differently
    ]
    
    for input_text, expected_plain in test_cases:
        tokens = list(_ansi_tokenize(input_text))
        plain = "".join(t.plain for t in tokens)
        print(f"Input: {repr(input_text)}, Plain: {repr(plain)}, Expected: {repr(expected_plain)}, Match: {plain == expected_plain}")

test_ansi_tokenize()

from rich.ansi import _ansi_tokenize

def test_ansi_paren():
    input_text = "Hello\x1b(World"
    tokens = list(_ansi_tokenize(input_text))
    plain = "".join(t.plain for t in tokens)
    print(f"Input: {repr(input_text)}, Plain: {repr(plain)}")

test_ansi_paren()

from rich.ansi import _ansi_tokenize

def test_ansi_strip():
    text = "Hello\x1b7World"
    tokens = list(_ansi_tokenize(text))
    plain = "".join(t.plain for t in tokens)
    print(f"Plain: {repr(plain)}")
    assert plain == "HelloWorld"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_ansi_strip()
